claim: Query recall ranks by similarity, not salience/recency: on 200 real prompts judged by qwen3.6 P(yes), similarity alone gave 0.62 precision at 1 injection/prompt vs 0.50 for the old sim*salience*recency*utility formula; every recency weight hurt. touch_memories must not refresh last_access, or injection keeps memories fresh forever (self-reinforcing loop that put lesson #1 in every brief). Hook --min-score 0.50 on query_score = same relevant hits (100 vs 96), 52 vs 96 irrelevant. Eval scripts: judge pool = top-8 by sim + each variant's top-3.

SessionStart hooks do not fire for subagents (only 1 of 135 subagent transcripts in a week had the scry mandate), so subagents grepped for ~90% of all code searches. Plugin context for subagents must come from a SubagentStart hook (hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName=SubagentStart, additionalContext); scry_watch.py handles it by injecting SEARCH_MANDATE only, with no watch, gc, or work brief.

Reranker input length on finance-query eval (BGE v2-m3, top 20, HyDE on): 1200 chars recall 0.783 p50 2.0s; 2000 chars 0.817 p50 2.1s; 3000 chars 0.833 p50 2.3s (reproduced twice); 6000 chars 0.817 p50 3.2s. Default max_chars = 3000 sits at the recall peak.

sqlite-vec 0.1.9 vec0 point lookups and rowid-IN-filtered KNN both read the whole 4 MB vector block per chunk, so a rescore from vec0 can never beat exact search; rescore from a plain rowid table instead

Float vectors live in the plain chunk_vectors rowid table (schema v3); vec0 holds only the binary vec_chunks_bit coarse index. Exact KNN is a Rust scan over chunk_vectors and the coarse rescore reads 4 KB rows from it; the v2->v3 migration is one-way, so deploy binary and service restart together
